name: IL-05
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Mike Quigley running with a large cash advantage
Republican challenger Tommy Hanson has reported no fundraising
model.rationale: Quigley holds a heavily Democratic Chicago-area seat, has over $1.1 million on hand, and faces an opponent with no visible fundraising, while markets price his win at 96%. The fundamentals point to a lopsided margin, so the forecast stays at Safe D.
model.watch: Any polling showing Hanson gaining traction or a major late outside-spending push against Quigley would be the first sign of movement.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Mike Quigley, a Democratic incumbent, is seeking another term in this Chicago-based House district, which leans Democratic by about 19 points. He has raised roughly $726,000 and holds about $1.2 million in cash, with no outside groups opposing him. His Republican challenger, Tommy Hanson, has no reported fundraising or cash on hand, and no outside spending has appeared on his behalf.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the money gap, and prediction markets, which price Quigley's chances at about 96 percent. The expected margin is roughly 25 points, consistent with a Safe Democratic rating, though the absence of polling leaves some room for uncertainty.
